extra.message: The NextAuth CredentialsProvider authorize() function validates credentials against hard-coded values: username 'user' and password 'password' (pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].js:26). Anyone who knows these fixed credentials can authenticate and receive a valid signed session JWT, completely bypassing authentication. There is no database lookup, rate limiting, or credential hashing.

Sensitive secrets are hard-coded directly in a client-side React component: an API key 'X92nJdsL8aQp03Mf' (line 15), a database connection string with embedded credentials 'mongodb://user:password@localhost:27017/db' (line 16), and private server endpoints (line 17). Because this is client-side code, Next.js compiles these values into the public JavaScript bundle, which is served from /_next/static — a path explicitly excluded from the authentication middleware matcher (middleware.js:47). Any user (even unauthenticated) can fetch the dashboard page bundle and extract the API key and database credentials.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: NEXTAUTH_SECRET is exposed via the `env` block in next.config.js. Variables declared in next.config.js `env` are inlined by webpack into ALL bundles, including the client-side JavaScript served to every browser — unlike .env files, which only expose NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables to the client. NEXTAUTH_SECRET is the HMAC signing secret for NextAuth session JWTs; anyone who extracts it from the public bundle can forge a valid session token, set the next-auth.session-token cookie, and pass the getToken() authentication check in middleware.js:23-33, bypassing authentication entirely.

extra.message: The Next.js configuration defines no `headers()` block, so the application is deployed without baseline security headers: no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors (clickjacking), no X-Content-Type-Options (MIME sniffing), no Strict-Transport-Security, and no Referrer-Policy.
